metadata.title: An integral regular summand in every staircase Specht tensor cube
metadata.description:
For every staircase partition rho=(m,m-1,...,1) of N=m(m+1)/2, we prove that the integral regular module Z[S_N] is a direct summand of (S_Z^rho)^{tensor 3}. Ordered row and column polytabloids give a tensor whose translates form a basis of that summand. A single integral coordinate functional gives an explicit equivariant retraction. The splitting survives base change to every commutative unital ring, including nonflat base change, with no restriction on the characteristic. The proof uses the separating-product mechanism of Bryant and Kovács, Ikenmeyer's triangular palette uniqueness, and a square-deficit calculation from the pinned cyclic-polytabloid construction.

 

This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent proof, contribution and manuscript reviews, not external peer review. Supporting Lean material is partial and does not formalize the complete theorem. Mathematical results from OpenAI/math at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises, with exact source interfaces and other credited inputs disclosed in the paper. The literature comparison is bounded and does not certify worldwide priority.

 

Formal coverage: Sixteen supporting Lean theorems prove conditional coordinate splitting, equivariance, injectivity, complement, scalar extension of given split maps and integer zero-deficit implication. The staircase-specific separation identity, polytabloids, palettes, support budget, unit sign, all-m instance and multiplicities remain prose proofs.

metadata.title: Dimension-free stability of binary-information contraction
metadata.description: Under the sharp contraction and joining results specified in the paper, we prove linear stability of binary-information contraction on every compact amplitude and correlation rectangle, uniformly over finite cube dimensions. For information psi(a) tending to zero, the constant grows at most as a to the power -4, and this exponent is necessary. The statements apply to arbitrary [-1,1]-valued kernels, without a mean restriction or a pointwise interior margin. We also strengthen the entropy-production inequality D(u) >= F(I(u)) by an absolute positive multiple of (E u) squared times I(u) squared. The proof combines strict Gaussian contraction, a compactness argument for joining laws, and estimates retaining the entropy of rare endpoint values.

metadata.title: A rooted entropy bound for perfect matchings
metadata.description: Let H_G(x) be the maximum entropy of a perfect-matching law with prescribed edge marginals x in a finite loopless multigraph. We prove that, for every vertex v, H_G(x) is at least -sum_e x_e log x_e + (3/2) sum_{e not incident to v} (1-x_e) log(1-x_e). On 2m vertices this gives a coefficient (3/2)(1-1/m) in the unrooted complementary-entropy bound. The proof reserves the contribution of one vertex star. This makes the entropy deficit exactly additive under contraction of a tight odd cut and permits induction before a covariance second-variation argument. Boundary marginals and labelled parallel edges are included. We also obtain lower bounds for weighted partition functions and for graphs containing edge-disjoint perfect matchings.

metadata.title: A superquadratic sensitivity separation for transitive Boolean functions
metadata.description:
For every C>0 we construct a nonconstant total Boolean function f, invariant under a group transitive on all input coordinates, with f(0)=0 and bs(f,0)>C s(f)^2, where s is ordinary sensitivity maximized over all inputs. We also obtain a fixed exponent alpha>2 and a sequence of such functions with bs(F_m,0)>=s(F_m)^alpha and diverging zero-input block sensitivity. The pinned OpenAI manuscript supplies the nested-predicate and sensitivity-recurrence framework. First-difference labels on a fixed-depth Paley tournament product simultaneously give a small label alphabet, a constant head-pattern exclusion bound and affine label covariance; these preserve transitivity on the full raw coordinate set while meeting the recurrence estimates. The manuscript includes all four profile bounds, zero-input blocks, balancing and the composition endpoint. Source architecture, earlier spectral/cyclotomic symmetry constructions and classical composition are credited. The accompanying Lean code verifies selected exclusion, affine-action and scalar-recurrence interfaces, not the full Boolean theorem. No optimal exponent or worldwide priority is claimed.

metadata.title: Sharp ball–tube and ball–slab nesting costs in the cubic three-torus
metadata.description: Assume the scalar isoperimetric profile and equality classification for the cubic flat three-torus stated in the paper. We determine the sharp summed-perimeter cost of nesting a ball-volume region inside a slightly thinned tube-volume or slab-volume region, minimizing over all finite-perimeter pairs. For ball–tube contact the minimum is asymptotic to K(R) epsilon squared, where K(R) = 4 pi R / (R + 4 G_R) and G_R = R squared - (R/2) cot(1/(2R)), for 2/9 < R < 1/pi. For ball–slab contact it is asymptotic to 2 pi epsilon squared / |log epsilon|, for 1/(2 pi) < R < 1/3. A common volume-correction flow gives scalar quasiminimality of exact paired minimizers. The sharp constants then follow from the coupled quadratic problem and logarithmic capacity at the two polar contacts.

metadata.title: Factor-count residues and Poisson-Dirichlet limits for prime predecessors
metadata.description: Assuming specified analytic estimates for shifted primes and Dirichlet L-functions, we prove that Ω(p−1) modulo any fixed positive integer is asymptotically uniform and independent of the ranked logarithmic prime factor sizes, for primes in each fixed reduced arithmetic progression. The factor-size limit is the Poisson–Dirichlet distribution with parameter one. For parity, we also obtain joint independence from the squarefree indicator, with its progression-dependent density. This gives the Moree–Hommersom parity conjecture under the same assumptions. The proof combines marked correlations with a principal-term model that is compatible with small-prime multiplication and the extraction of prime arguments.

metadata.title: Weighted capacity for four-state reconstruction with variable edge channels
metadata.description: Assuming a specified moment-saving inequality for a preserved class of four-state posterior laws, we characterize reconstruction on deterministic locally finite trees with variable symmetric ferromagnetic edge channels by positivity of a weighted nonlinear capacity. The channel parameters may approach either zero or one, and perfectly transmitting edges are allowed. We give quantitative comparisons between capacity and limiting posterior information with constants independent of the tree, its degrees, and the edge parameters. The proof uses local posterior estimates valid without channel smoothing and a flow estimate controlled by branch splitting. The capacity is unchanged by replacing a chain by its composite channel; on a ray, it gives the exact criterion that the product of the channel parameters is positive.

metadata.title: Exact discrete logarithms from a flagged polygonal transform
metadata.description: Assume the flagged polygonal-transform and exact-factoring interfaces specified in the paper. We construct a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family over one fixed finite gate set that computes discrete logarithms in prime fields with probability one and polynomial worst-case resources. For prime-order inputs, each verified Fourier-bin label has probability at least 1/(81q). Given its verified logarithm, that probability is computable exactly by a bounded number of lattice-point counts in dimension at most thirteen. Dyadic completion produces success probability exactly one quarter, followed by one exact amplification step. All sampled probabilities are dyadic; no input-dependent rotation or postselection is used.

metadata.title: The Borsuk number of the complex projective plane is nine
metadata.description:
For the rank-one projector realization of the complex projective plane in the eight-dimensional affine space of trace-one Hermitian matrices with the Frobenius metric, we prove diameter sqrt(2) and Borsuk number exactly nine. The lower bound covers arbitrary subsets. A covariant perturbation of the nine Hesse rays, controlled by a uniform two-trio estimate in complex neighborhoods, yields nine compact sets of strictly smaller diameter and nine Fubini–Study balls of radius below pi/4 covering the whole space. This attains d+1 in dimension eight. The accompanying Lean development formalizes supporting scalar inequalities and complex identities, not the full geometric and topological theorem.

metadata.title: Scalar extremizers for complete Crouzeix equality in dimension four
metadata.description: Assume the complete Crouzeix bound and the analytic Faber coefficient estimate stated in the paper. Let A be a complex matrix of order at most four, and let P be a matrix-valued polynomial of arbitrary finite degree and coefficient size. If ||P[A]|| = 2 max_{W(A)} ||P|| > 0, we prove that there are constant unit coefficient vectors u, v for which p = v* P u attains the same equality. Jin's scalar rigidity theorem then implies that W(A) is a disk, and the extracted scalar polynomial is a monomial after centering and scaling that disk. The main step converts zero slack in a positive boundary-field inequality into a rank-one condition on the coefficient factors of extremal singular vectors. An elementary Hermitian-pencil argument supplies the required regular boundary arc in dimension four.

metadata.title: A quadratic-density lower bound for tetrahedral cylinder covers
metadata.description: Let T be a regular tetrahedron and let A_min(T) be the least area of an orthogonal projection of T onto a plane. We prove that every finite cover of T by cylinders with measurable perpendicular bases B_i satisfies sum_i |B_i| >= (sqrt(15)/9) A_min(T). The proof computes the largest line integral of a radial quadratic density on T. We also prove that sqrt(15)/9 is the best constant obtainable from any nonnegative polynomial density of degree at most two by dividing its mass by a uniform bound on its line integrals. This optimality concerns the density method within that class, rather than the cylinder-covering infimum.
references: K. Bezdek and A. E. Litvak, Covering convex bodies by cylinders and lattice points by flats, Journal of Geometric Analysis 19 (2009), no. 2, 233-243. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12220-008-9063-6.

metadata.title: Quantum verification of full-continuum Coulomb energy with unit nuclei
metadata.description:
We prove uniform QMA membership for the spectral-infimum decision problem for the full spinful antisymmetric Coulomb Hamiltonian with unit nuclei, distinct rational nuclear positions, unary electron number and inverse-polynomial promise gap. Nuclear repulsion is omitted. Positions and thresholds use binary rational encoding; the result assumes neither binding nor a spectral gap, geometric separation, bounded physical diameter, a selected finite basis, a fixed spin sector or an efficiently prepared low-energy state. The proof combines quantitative localization including escaped electrons, Hardy-controlled Coulomb caps, a finite kinetic cutoff, exact shifted sampling with L2 error control, and a polynomial-size verifier on arbitrary witness states. Together with the hardness theorem of the pinned source manuscript, this gives QMA completeness for the same problem. Classical sector localization, finite-basis electronic complexity, smooth-box discretization and earlier real-space simulation estimates are credited. The accompanying Lean support proves selected finite sampling, representation-average and scalar error interfaces; it does not formalize the full continuum or quantum-complexity theorem. metadata.title: Fourth-moment comparison of zero-field SK free-energy fluctuations

metadata.title: The crossing number of the complete graph minus an edge
metadata.description:
We prove that for every integer n >= 2 and every edge e of the complete graph K_n, the ordinary crossing number is cr(K_n-e) = (1/4) floor((n+2)/2) floor((n-1)/2) floor((n-3)/2) floor((n-4)/2), which was conjectured by Zheng, Lin, Yang and Cui in 2007. The proof relies on the September 2026 OpenAI preprint proving the Harary–Hill formula for cr(K_n), whose stated results we use without re-proving them. Given that formula, the even orders follow from a theorem of Ouyang, Wang and Huang (2014), equivalently of Chia and Lee (2015), and the odd orders n <= 13 follow from their counting bound and integrality. The new content is the lower bound for odd n >= 15. We adapt the polynomial rank method of the OpenAI preprint to the missing edge. The adaptation restricts the test polynomials so that they put no weight on the missing pair. It pairs two different vanishing subspaces by mixed orthogonality. It also localizes, with a twisted detector that needs the full rectangular nonsingularity statement of the preprint, only at the vertices whose stars are complete. Via the product identity of Ouyang, Wang and Huang, the formula gives the crossing number of K_m square P_n conjectured by Zheng et al. for all m >= 4 and n >= 1, where P_n is the path with n edges. The new lower-bound input enters this consequence for odd m >= 13 and n >= 2; the literature comparison is bounded as stated in the novelty section of the paper.

metadata.title: Disk rigidity for attained complete polynomial Crouzeix equality
metadata.description:
Relative to the pinned complete Crouzeix inequality and its exterior Faber operations, and to Jin's geometric circle criterion, we prove that actual factor-two equality for one finite matrix-valued polynomial forces the numerical range to be a nondegenerate disk in every finite dimension. metadata.title: A conditional power stability estimate for the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality
metadata.description: Assuming the smooth variance and moment-coordinate identities specified in this paper, we prove a power stability estimate for the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality on origin-symmetric convex bodies. In each dimension at least three, a small deficit forces the two bodies close in Hausdorff distance to independent positive dilations of common complementary factors. The exponent depends only on dimension; the constant also depends on fixed inner and outer radii and on an interior range of interpolation parameters. No boundary regularity, common reflection group, facet bound, or lower bound on block angles is required. The proof retains nonzero derivative energy in a compact-target moment limit, converts a weak boundary identity to an absolute flux estimate, and constructs one product body whose two dilations approximate the original endpoints. The exponent is explicit but not sharp.

metadata.title: Dimension-uniform coefficient extraction from nonlinear curl
metadata.description: Let L(x) = sum_r x_r X_r, where the X_r are real symmetric m by m matrices and sum_r X_r^2 is bounded above by K times the identity for a fixed finite K. For the Gaussian inverse Mills ratio q, we prove that the mean squared row curl of q(L) controls both the lack of full symmetry of the coefficient tensor and the sum of all squared coefficient commutators. After division by m, the estimate has a modulus independent of the dimension, bounded by C_K/log(e/t) when the normalized curl energy t is small. The proof compares divided differences at x and -x and controls a cutoff on all tensor indices by Gaussian operator moments. We also construct a fully symmetric tensor with a controlled operator-energy bound and controlled algebraic residual.
